decision.what_is_decided: Whether a candidate model answer fully and correctly covers the last user request, without inventing ungiven context or padding with filler.

inputs.name: request
inputs.source: last user-role message in the conversation, truncated
inputs.role: the ask the answer is judged against

inputs.name: answer
inputs.source: provider completion text passed into askGate, truncated
inputs.role: candidate reply being scored for adequacy

decision.downstream_action: Score is compared to a threshold; fail rejects the attempt and retries the next model, pass serves this answer.

jev_questions.what_it_asks: Whether the candidate answer fully and correctly covers the last user request, with no invented context and no filler.

semantic_ambiguity.evidence: Adequacy bundles completeness, correctness, invention, and filler on open-ended request and answer text; those criteria have no unique surface form.

context_dependence.evidence: The same answer is judged only relative to the last user request; askGate strips the rest of the conversation so the verdict is pair-specific.

deterministic_expressibility.evidence: No stable tokens or structure define full coverage, invention, or padding across arbitrary tasks; an exact checker would itself be open-ended NLU.

judgment_required.evidence: The noul is a yes/no quality reading of two free-form texts; comments call it a narrow judgment whose definition lives in the yes/no criteria.

rule_stability.evidence: What counts as fully, invented, or filler shifts with request type even though the criteria text is fixed in GATE_QUESTIONS.

risk_or_policy_component.evidence: The gate scores answer adequacy for retry, not harm, safety, or compliance; safety-sensitive routing lives in a different question set.

natural_language_understanding.evidence: Both state fields are truncated natural-language request and answer; the noul must read them as language, not structured fields.

decision_complexity.evidence: One noul, but it jointly judges coverage, correctness, hallucination, and verbosity rather than a single surface property.

why_jev_hypotheses.evidence: GATE_QUESTIONS asks whether answer fully and correctly covers request; askGate feeds those two texts to systemOne (src/signals.ts:133-144).
Request and answer are free-form truncated strings; yes/no criteria interpret missing parts, invention, and filler in that pair (src/signals.ts:133-144).
Noul is graded yes vs no; complete maps fail to retry the next candidate and pass to serve this answer (src/router.ts:209-215).
No counts, equality, or schema checks; comments and noul criteria define a quality judgment of the reply (src/signals.ts:131-144).
Criteria are answer-quality tests for a retry gate, not organizational, legal, or product-policy rules (src/signals.ts:131-136, src/router.ts:206-214).
The score is used only as pass/fail quality for fallback, not to estimate harm or safety risk (src/router.ts:204-215).
Addresses is a yes/no class of the answer that is only meaningful given the last user request as context (src/signals.ts:142-144).
Open-ended request/answer pairs plus completeness, invention, and filler cannot be captured by stable lexical or structural rules (src/signals.ts:133-144).
Criteria text is fixed in GATE_QUESTIONS; the repo does not show whether those criteria are treated as evolving or tunable policy.
Inputs are concrete truncated strings from messages and the completion; uncertainty is in the judgment, not missing or noisy input values (src/signals.ts:142-144).
Verdict depends on the request-answer pair; complete also applies the gate only for configured tiers with a remaining fallback and no tool calls (src/signals.ts:142-144, src/router.ts:205-206).
A non-Jev checker would need general NLU for coverage, invention, and padding on arbitrary tasks, which would be brittle next to one noul (src/signals.ts:131-144).

not_reasons.note: Gate is optional, default-limited to some tiers, skipped when no fallback or when tool calls exist; criticality is not why Jev is used.
No evidence Jev replaces a slow check; the gate itself is billed per input token and adds latency to the attempt.
askGate is a short linear helper; size does not explain the Jev call.
askGate has no branching; branching lives in the caller around an already-made score.
The gate is a product feature, but the repo does not show that feature importance is why Jev was chosen.
The Jev site is a small call with one question; code complexity is not the reason.

observed.claim: askGate calls systemOne with GATE_QUESTIONS on truncated last-user request text and truncated answer text.

evidence.observation: Last user message and answer are sliced into state; systemOne is invoked with GATE_QUESTIONS.

observed.claim: The only gate question is a noul named addresses that judges whether the answer fully and correctly covers the request, using yes/no criteria for completeness, no invention, and no filler.

evidence.observation: GATE_QUESTIONS defines one noul whose criteria spell those quality conditions.

observed.claim: complete treats the noul as a pass/fail gate against a threshold and on failure retries the next model.

evidence.observation: askGate result is compared to threshold; failure records a gate error and continues to the next candidate.

observed.claim: The gate runs only when enabled, the attempt tier is in the configured set, a later candidate exists, and the completion has no tool calls.

evidence.observation: Gate flag, tier set, and threshold are read from config.
askGate is skipped unless those conditions and empty tool-calls hold.

inferred.claim: Jev is here because deciding answer adequacy is a semantic reading of two free-form texts, not a computable equality or metric.

evidence.observation: A noul over request and answer, with qualitative yes/no criteria, is the entire decision.

inferred.claim: Exact matching or heuristics would miss paraphrase, partial coverage, invented context, and padding on varied tasks.

evidence.observation: State is arbitrary NL slices; criteria name qualities that are not surface-detectable.

unknown: Why the developer chose Jev rather than heuristics or another judge.
Why noul rather than score, and why the default threshold and default gated tier.
Whether the yes/no criteria were tuned empirically or how accurate the gate is.

deterministic_alternative.what_rules_would_need: Parse the last user request into required parts, check the answer covers each correctly, detect invented ungiven context, and detect padding on trivial asks, across arbitrary natural-language tasks.
deterministic_alternative.adequacy: Fragile or impossible: request and answer forms are open-ended, fully and correctly are task-dependent, and invention or filler have no stable pattern. A deterministic checker would be a second NLU system that still misses paraphrase and implicit requirements.
